verdicts.decision_note: The message establishes the software acceptance condition that commission earnings remain numerically consistent between dashboard totals and per-NFT detail views.
First concrete failure: the same account showed $5, $0, and $5,000,000 for commission earnings across different views.
Target-specific implementation claim after the failure: the freelancer reports that total and per-NFT earnings data were corrected.
The client changes the accounting data rule to one commission per primary mint, excludes secondary sales, and requires randomly awarded commissions to register.
First concrete no-referral-path failure: only four commissions were registered across seven mints.
Target-specific implementation claim that missing commission records were backfilled after the no-referral undercount.
The client requires randomly awarded no-code commissions to be projected in dashboard and NFT-attribute data.
The accepted manual-finalization flow changes the executable trigger at which a no-code random commission is registered.
Post-claim persistence on the projection path: sent no-code commissions remained absent from the leaderboard and NFT attributes.

value_updates.commission_count_basis: One $5 commission must be accounted for per completed primary mint, whether or not a referral code is used; secondary-market sales are excluded.
value_updates.no_code_commission_projection: Randomly assigned $5 commissions from no-referral mints must be reflected on the dashboard, leaderboard, and in NFT attributes.
value_updates.commission_view_consistency: Awarded $5 commissions from both code-used and no-code mints must be represented accurately and consistently in dashboard summaries, leaderboards, and per-NFT attributes.
value_updates.ticket_commission_consistency_rule: Every issued ticket corresponds to one $5 commission, so ticket and commission totals must remain consistent.

verdicts.decision_note: The client sets the $5-per-primary-mint accounting rule, no-code projection, cross-view consistency, and historical backfill condition; unchanged scope dimensions are normalized to null.
The client removes the executable historical commission-backfill obligation while retaining correct forward accounting.
The client accepts the first-mint exception, changing commission-count logic because no earlier NFT holder exists.
Target-specific implementation claim after persistent failure: temporary backend logic for reflecting commissions was implemented.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Yes, I'm happy with that logic.

Right now, after 12 mints, the leader board displays 11 tickets and 11 commissions. Perfect.

However!

The attributes for the NFT still aren't quite right.

My screenshots show the following:

On the leaderboard, NFT #5 displays 2 tickets and 2 x $5 commissions, which is perfect.

After I click NFT #5, the top of the page shows 2 tickets & 2 referrals, also perfect.

However, its attributes still display 1 referral and total earnings of only $5.

execution.observed_behavior: After the backend implementation claim, the leaderboard showed 11 commissions and NFT #5 showed two $5 commissions, but that NFT's attributes still displayed total earnings of only $5.
